title: Restoring the name of a struck-off company
law: Section 252(1) and Section 252(3), Companies Act, 2013 (read with Section 248)
summary: Gets a company's name put back on the Register of Companies by applying to the NCLT after the Registrar struck it off.
when: The Registrar has removed the company's name under Section 248 and the company, a member, a creditor or a workman wants it back.
applies: All companies (private companies have no special exemption)

steps.t: Check who can apply and by when
steps.d: A person aggrieved by the Registrar's dissolution order can appeal to the NCLT within three years of that order. The company, or any member, creditor or workman, can apply within twenty years of the Gazette notice under Section 248(5). The NCLT restores the name if removal was not justified.
steps.time: 3 years from the order, or 20 years from the Gazette notice

steps.d: The application must explain why the company was struck off, the grounds, proof of business or a good reason for no business, and the harm to members, creditors or workmen. Gather the supporting file listed in the checklist.
docs: Covering letters to NCLT and ROC
Index, synopsis, list of dates and events
Board resolutions, authority letter and power of attorney

steps.t: Approve the filing at a board meeting
steps.d: Pass a board resolution to file the appeal under Section 252, authorise one director to sign it and appoint experts. Pass a second resolution (with a letter of authority and power of attorney) authorising the Company Secretary to appear before the NCLT.

Type or print in double spacing on one side of petition paper, with margins of about 4 cm top, 5 cm left and 2.5 cm right. Paginate, index and stitch it as a paper book. The authorised director signs every page. Notarise the application, affidavits and annexures, and number every page in series.

Make two photocopies of the signed and notarised set on petition paper. The reference note asks for copies on green paper and also on white paper; confirm the NCLT bench's current practice before copying.

steps.t: Serve a copy on the Registrar
steps.d: Send a copy of the application to the ROC by registered post AD, by courier or by hand. Keep the proof of delivery.

Number the final set and attach proof of service on the ROC. Scan it in grey scale at 300 DPI, put the authorised director's DSC on the last page of each document, bookmark it and make it text-searchable (OCR). If a file is over 100 MB, split it into volumes of at most 200 pages each. Physical and online volumes must match.
Register on the NCLT e-filing portal as a Company Secretary user, upload the application and pay the NCLT fee of Rs. 1,000 online.
Prepare three physical sets. File two with the NCLT: the signed original in volumes and a photocopy. Get an acknowledgement on the third set for your records.

Track the hearing date on the portal and check the cause list the evening before. Attend online or in person. The ROC or other authorities may reply before or at the hearing. Be ready to argue and to give evidence. The NCLT looks at whether the company was doing business and whether restoring it is just and fair.

If satisfied, the NCLT orders the name restored. It may set conditions such as paying penalties and filing all overdue returns and financial statements. Apply for a certified copy of the order and pay any fees and penalty set by the NCLT, keeping the challan.

steps.t: File the order with the Registrar
steps.d: File the certified copy with proof of payment in Form INC-28. The ROC then restores the name and updates the register.
steps.time: Within 30 days of receiving the certified copy

steps.d: File all pending annual returns and financial statements and pay all pending dues and penalties.
steps.time: The reference note says within 30 days of restoration

forms.purpose: Registrar's notice of striking off, attached to the application
General appeal or application to the Tribunal (as named in the reference note)
forms.deadline: Within 3 years of the order, or 20 years of the Gazette notice

forms.purpose: Affidavit verifying the petition
Memorandum of appearance
Filing the NCLT order with the Registrar
forms.deadline: Within 30 days of receiving the certified copy

forms.purpose: Pending annual returns
forms.deadline: Per source, within 30 days of restoration

forms.purpose: Pending financial statements
forms.deadline: Per source, within 30 days of restoration

checklist: Strike-off notice (STK-7) and Gazette notice date noted
Audited financial statements for the relevant years
Proof the company was operating (invoices, bank statements, GST and tax filings, agreements)
Board resolution to appeal and authorise a director
Board resolution, authority letter and power of attorney for the Company Secretary
Affidavit and NCLT forms signed and notarised
Covering letters to NCLT and ROC

meetings.title: Board meeting to approve the restoration application
meetings.notice_days: At least 7 days (shorter if allowed by the Act and the articles)

resolutions.title: Filing the appeal for restoration and authorising a director
resolutions.text:
RESOLVED THAT an appeal / application be filed before the National Company Law Tribunal, [name of bench] Bench, under Section 252 of the Companies Act, 2013 for restoration of the name of {co} in the Register of Companies, the name having been struck off by the Registrar of Companies on [date].

RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director], Director, be authorised to sign, verify and file the appeal, affidavits and all related papers, to engage such experts and advisers as needed, and to do all things necessary for this purpose.

resolutions.title: Authorising the Company Secretary to appear before the NCLT
resolutions.text:
RESOLVED THAT [name], Company Secretary (Membership No. [number]), be authorised to appear and represent {co} before the National Company Law Tribunal in the appeal under Section 252 of the Companies Act, 2013, to file papers, make submissions and receive orders on its behalf.

RESOLVED FURTHER THAT a letter of authority and a power of attorney be issued to him / her for this purpose, and that [name of director], Director, be authorised to sign them.

docs.title: Covering letter to the Registrar of Companies
paras: To, The Registrar of Companies, [city].
Sub: Copy of appeal for restoration of the name of {co} (CIN [CIN]) under Section 252 of the Companies Act, 2013.

Please find enclosed a copy of the appeal / application filed before the National Company Law Tribunal, [name of bench] Bench, with annexures, for restoring the name of {co} to the Register of Companies. Kindly acknowledge receipt.
For {co}, [name of director], Director, DIN [DIN]. Date: [date]. Place: [place].

docs.title: Affidavit in support of the application
paras: I, [name], son / daughter of [name], aged [age], director of {co}, do solemnly affirm and state as follows.

1. I am authorised by the board to make this affidavit. 2. The facts stated in the application are true to my knowledge and belief, based on the records of the company. 3. The company was carrying on business [or had reasonable cause for not doing so, state it] at the time of the strike-off. 4. The annexures are true copies of the originals.
Deponent. Verification: Verified at [place] on [date] that the contents of this affidavit are true and nothing is concealed.

flags: The reference note gives the one-year-style limits as three years (appeal under Section 252(1)) and twenty years (Section 252(3)). This matches the Act as amended in 2019, but check the current text before relying on it.
The reference note names NCLT Form 9 for the application. The NCLT Rules, 2016 usually use Form NCLT-1 for applications and petitions; verify the form the registry accepts.
The reference note asks for both green-paper and white-paper photocopies in the same step with near-identical words. Treat as unclear and check the bench's practice.
The 30-day limit for post-restoration returns is not in Section 252. The NCLT order usually sets the deadline; follow the order.
STK-7 is the Registrar's notice that the name is struck off, not an order; confirm which document the bench wants.

title: Adjudication of penalties by the Registrar
law: Section 454, Companies Act, 2013; Companies (Adjudication of Penalties) Rules, 2014
summary: Explains how the Adjudicating Officer imposes a monetary penalty on a company or officer and how to reply, appear and appeal.
when: A company or officer has broken a provision where the Act sets only a penalty, not a fine or jail term, and receives a show-cause notice.
applies: All companies; a private company must follow every step

steps.d: It applies where the Act sets only a penalty for the breach, not a fine or imprisonment.

The Adjudicating Officer (the Registrar) sends a notice to the company, the officer in default or any other person, asking why the penalty should not be imposed. It states the breach alleged, the penal provisions and the maximum penalty for the company and each officer.
The notice must allow at least 15 days and at most 30 days from service to show cause. The officer may extend the period case by case.
Reply only in electronic mode within the time in the notice. Authorise someone at a board meeting to prepare and file the reply, and ask for more time in writing if needed.

If the officer wants a personal appearance, or you ask to be heard, the officer sends a notice fixing a date. This notice goes out within 10 working days of getting your reply. You may appear in person or through an authorised representative.
steps.time: Notice within 10 working days of the reply

steps.d: After a fair hearing the officer passes a written order with reasons. The order is due within 30 days of the notice if no appearance is needed or no reply comes, and within 90 days of the notice if there is a hearing.

The order is dated and signed and states why appearance was needed. If someone does not reply or does not appear, the officer may impose the penalty without them after recording reasons. Where the Act sets a fixed sum, that sum is imposed.

Copies of the order go to the company, officer or person concerned and to the Central Government, and the order is put on the website. Pay the penalty through the MCA portal. All penalties go to the Consolidated Fund of India.
Appeal in writing to the Regional Director having jurisdiction, in Form ADJ, with the grounds and a certified copy of the order.
steps.time: Within 60 days of receiving the order

forms.purpose: Appeal to the Regional Director against the adjudication order
forms.deadline: Within 60 days of receiving the order

checklist: Show-cause notice and date of service noted
Board authority for officer to reply
Facts and records of the alleged default collected
Penalty paid on MCA portal and challan kept

meetings.title: Board meeting to authorise reply to show-cause notice

resolutions.title: Authorising reply to show-cause notice
resolutions.text:
RESOLVED THAT the show-cause notice dated [date] received from the Adjudicating Officer under Section 454 of the Companies Act, 2013 regarding alleged non-compliance with Section [section] be noted.

RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name], [designation], be authorised to prepare and file the reply in electronic mode, to seek extension of time, to appear before the Adjudicating Officer, and to appoint a professional to represent {co} in this matter.

docs.title: Reply to show-cause notice
paras: To, The Adjudicating Officer / Registrar of Companies, [city]. Ref: Notice No. [number] dated [date] under Section 454 of the Companies Act, 2013.

{co} (CIN [CIN]) submits that [state facts of the alleged default and reasons, e.g. delay due to ...]. The default, if any, was not wilful and has been corrected on [date] by filing [form / document].
In view of this, it is requested that no penalty be imposed or that a lenient view be taken. {co} also requests a personal hearing, if the officer considers it necessary.
For {co}, [name], [designation]. Date: [date].

flags: The reference note does not mention that for small companies, one person companies, producer companies and start-ups the penalty is lower (Section 446B). Check whether this applies.
The reference note says the Adjudicating Officer is the Registrar. Adjudicating Officers are appointed by the Central Government (usually Registrars). Verify the officer named in the notice.
Failure to pay the penalty can itself attract further action under Section 454(8); the reference note does not mention this.
private: A private company must follow all the steps.

title: Fast track merger without the NCLT
law: Section 233, Companies Act, 2013; Rule 25, Companies (Compromises, Arrangements and Amalgamations) Rules, 2016
summary: Merges two small companies, or a holding company and its wholly owned subsidiary, with approval of the Regional Director instead of the NCLT.
when: Two or more small companies want to merge, or a holding company wants to merge with its wholly owned subsidiary.
applies: Small companies; holding and wholly owned subsidiary (private or public)

steps.d: Each company's board approves the draft scheme. Prepare the draft scheme as it will be put to members and creditors, and the auditor's certificate on accounting treatment. File the board resolution with the ROC.
steps.time: Day X; MGT-14 within 30 days of the resolution

steps.d: Both companies send a notice in Form CAA.9 to the Regional Director, ROC, Official Liquidator, income tax authorities and creditors, inviting objections and suggestions within 30 days of the notice.
File audited financial statements and any other information the Official Liquidator asks for.
Obtain consent letters on the creditors' own letterhead, together with the scheme.
Each company files a declaration of solvency in Form CAA.10 with its ROC, with the fee. Attach the board resolution, a statement of assets and liabilities and the auditor's report on that statement.
Answer any queries or objections from authorities or parties during the 30-day period.

Send notice of the members' and creditors' meetings (creditors only if not dispensed) giving 21 days' notice, or shorter if all members consent. Attach a statement on the scheme, its effect on key managerial personnel, promoters, non-promoters and creditors, directors' material interests, the solvency declaration and a copy of the scheme.

Members holding at least 90% of the total number of shares must approve the scheme. Creditors representing nine-tenths in value must also approve. Obtain a scrutiniser's report. File the resolutions with the ROC.

steps.t: File the result with the authorities
steps.d: The transferee company files the report of the meeting results and the approved scheme in Form CAA.11 with the Regional Director, ROC and Official Liquidator, with proof of the notice sent to them. Also file the matter with the ROC through the MCA system as required.
steps.time: Within 7 days of the meetings; about X + 62

steps.d: Follow up for no-objection from the regulators.

If the ROC or Official Liquidator objects, or the Central Government thinks the scheme harms creditors or the public interest, an application is made to the NCLT in Form CAA.13 to consider the scheme under Section 232.
steps.time: Within 60 days of receiving the scheme

steps.d: If there is no objection, the Regional Director issues the confirmation order in Form CAA.12.

steps.t: File the order with the ROC
steps.d: Both companies file the confirmation order with their ROC in Form INC-28 with the fee.
steps.time: Within 30 days of receiving the order; about X + 105

forms.purpose: Board resolution and members' resolution on the scheme
Notice inviting objections and suggestions
Declaration of solvency
Report of meeting results with the scheme
Filing through the MCA system as named in the reference note
Confirmation order issued by the Regional Director
Application to the NCLT if authorities object
forms.deadline: Within 60 days of receiving the scheme

forms.purpose: Filing the confirmation order with the ROC
forms.deadline: Within 30 days of receiving the order

checklist: Check both companies qualify (small companies, or holding and wholly owned subsidiary)
Statement of assets and liabilities with auditor's report
Notice and explanatory statement for meetings
Proof of notice to RD, ROC and OL

General meeting of members to approve the scheme

resolutions.title: Approval of the scheme of amalgamation
resolutions.text:
RESOLVED THAT the scheme of amalgamation of [transferor company] with {co} under Section 233 of the Companies Act, 2013 and Rule 25 of the Companies (Compromises, Arrangements and Amalgamations) Rules, 2016, with effect from the appointed date of [date], in the form placed before the meeting, be approved.

RESOLVED FURTHER THAT notice in Form CAA.9 be sent to the Registrar of Companies, the Official Liquidator, income tax authorities and creditors, and that [name of director] be authorised to file the forms and do all things needed for this scheme.

resolutions.title: Declaration of solvency
resolutions.text:
RESOLVED THAT the Statement of Assets and Liabilities of {co} as on [date], with the auditor's report, be approved.

RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the directors make a declaration of solvency in Form CAA.10 that the company has made a full enquiry into its affairs and has no debts it cannot pay, and that [name of director] file it with the Registrar of Companies with the prescribed fee.

resolutions.title: Approval of the scheme by members
resolutions.text:
RESOLVED THAT the scheme of amalgamation of [transferor company] with {co}, in the form placed before the meeting, under Section 233 of the Companies Act, 2013, be approved.

RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the Board be authorised to accept any change the Regional Director or other authority may require and to do all acts needed to give effect to the scheme.
resolutions.explanatory: Explanatory statement: the scheme proposes to merge [transferor company] into {co} from [date]. Key terms: share exchange ratio [ratio]; effect on key managerial personnel, promoters, non-promoters and creditors [details]; directors' interest in the scheme [details]. Declaration of solvency and the auditor's report on assets and liabilities are attached. The scheme needs approval of members holding at least 90% of the total number of shares.

docs.title: Letter seeking creditor's consent
paras: To, [name of creditor], [address]. Sub: Scheme of amalgamation of [transferor company] with {co} under Section 233.
We enclose a copy of the scheme. Under the scheme your debt of Rs. [amount] will continue to be due from [transferee company] on the same terms. We request your written consent on your letterhead.
For {co}, [name], Director. Date: [date].

flags: The reference note applies the fast track route to both merger and demerger. Section 233 covers only merger or amalgamation (small companies, holding and wholly owned subsidiary, and start-ups merging with a small company or start-up). A demerger generally needs the NCLT route under Sections 230-232.
The reference note omits the start-up case and does not state the size limits that make a company small. Check the current definition in Section 2(85) and the notified limits.
Section C.3 speaks of 90% in value of shareholders. Rule 25 says members holding at least 90% of the total number of shares, and creditors representing nine-tenths in value.
The timeline is inconsistent: the Regional Director step shows X + 92 and the CAA.13 step shows X + 122, out of order. Use the statutory periods, not the table days.
The reference note lists a Form GNL-1 filing; check whether CAA.11 can be filed on its own.
private: Fast track merger (Section 233) is open only to small companies, holding and wholly owned subsidiary companies, and start-ups. Other private companies go to the NCLT under Sections 230 to 232. Under the fast track route: the Regional Director approves instead of the NCLT; the company holds its own meetings with no Tribunal chairperson or scrutinizer; members approve by 90% in value and creditors by a majority in number representing nine-tenths in value; objections go to the Regional Director, the Registrar or the Official Liquidator within 30 days; notice to SEBI applies only to listed companies; and the valuation report can be simpler between a wholly owned subsidiary and its parent. Other private companies need the full NCLT process and a detailed valuation by a registered valuer.

title: Main board IPO roadmap
law: Sections 13, 14, 18, 23, 32, 42, 61, 62, 63, 117, 129, 134, 149, 177, 188 and Schedule III, Companies Act, 2013; SEBI ICDR Regulations; SEBI LODR Regulations
summary: A phase-by-phase path from deciding to list to post-listing compliance on the NSE or BSE main board.
when: A company plans to raise money from the public and list its shares on the main board.
applies: Public companies (private companies must convert first)

steps.d: Assess why you want an IPO, align promoters on dilution and control, check revenues, profits and net worth against ICDR and exchange eligibility, review group structure and related-party dealings, plan investor exits by offer for sale, and clean up tax and legal issues. Plan any pre-IPO placement with pricing and disclosure rules in mind.

Appoint a SEBI-registered Category-I merchant banker as lead manager, a peer-reviewed statutory auditor for restated financials (3 to 5 years), company and lead-manager legal advisers, a registrar to the issue, bankers and escrow bankers, and PR or IR firms. An internal project office and secretarial adviser are optional. Sign engagement letters and set a master calendar.

Convert to a public company and alter the MOA and AOA. Add independent directors and form the Audit, Nomination and Remuneration, CSR, Stakeholders Relationship and Risk Management committees where applicable. Appoint Company Secretary (compliance officer), CFO and CEO. Meet promoter contribution and lock-in rules, and dematerialise 100% of pre-IPO shares. Verify beneficial ownership and finalise the ESOP policy if any.
docs: Resolutions for conversion and alteration of MOA and AOA

steps.d: Run legal, financial, corporate, business, FEMA, labour and internal-control reviews in parallel. Move eligible unclaimed dividends and shares (over 7 years) to IEPF, adopt a litigation materiality policy, review ESG factors, and collect no-objection letters from bankers, charge holders, landlords and regulators. The merchant banker prepares the draft red herring prospectus (DRHP).

File ROC forms for conversion, authorised capital increase, MOA and AOA changes and restructuring before the DRHP. Update PAN, TAN, GST, address, IEC and MSME records, and renew or update operational licences such as pollution consents, factory licence, shops registration, FSSAI or drug licence and fire NOC.

Obtain a valuation report where FEMA or the Act needs one, finish the ESOP scheme, move IP and brand assets to the company, amend or end shareholder or JV agreements that conflict with listing rules, sign agreements with NSDL, CDSL, exchanges, RTA and escrow banks, and settle the objects of the issue and risk factors.

steps.t: File the DRHP and get exchange approval
steps.d: Appoint a monitoring agency if the issue is above Rs. 100 crore. Activate the ISIN. File the DRHP with SEBI through the merchant banker and answer SEBI's observations within the review period. Apply to BSE or NSE for in-principle listing approval.
Run investor roadshows, fix the price band with the merchant banker, plan an optional anchor book, run the PR plan, reach retail and HNI investors and set up an IPO microsite.

File the final red herring prospectus with the ROC and SEBI. Keep the issue open at least 3 working days, with ASBA applications. Fix the issue price through book building, finalise the basis of allotment, credit demat accounts, refund excess money, and get listing and trading approval within 6 working days of issue close.
steps.time: Listing within 6 working days of close, per the reference note

steps.d: Follow SEBI LODR: financial results, board meeting and shareholding disclosures, SCORES grievance handling, insider trading code and trading window, annual report and AGM, periodic compliance certificates, and analyst and investor communication.

[amount] each, by fresh issue and / or offer for sale by existing shareholders, and list them on [BSE Limited / National Stock Exchange of India Limited], subject to approval of members, SEBI and other authorities.

[amount] each of {co} to the public through an initial public offer, and to list them on [stock exchange(s)].

resolutions.explanatory: Explanatory statement: the company proposes to raise funds by an initial public offer to [purpose, e.g. fund expansion and reduce debt]. The objects of the issue, size, and use of proceeds are set out in [details]. The directors recommend the resolution.

resolutions.text:
RESOLVED THAT, under Sections 13, 14 and 18 of the Companies Act, 2013, {co} be converted from a private limited company to a public limited company, its name be changed to [new name] Limited, and the Memorandum and Articles of Association be altered to reflect public company status and SEBI LODR requirements, in the form placed before the meeting.

resolutions.explanatory: Explanatory statement: conversion to a public company is needed to list. The alterations remove private company restrictions and add listing-related provisions. Copies of the altered MOA and AOA are open for inspection.

flags: The reference note says listing within 6 working days of issue close. Current SEBI rules require listing within 3 working days (T+3) of issue close; verify before planning.
The reference note does not state the core eligibility tests under ICDR Regulation 6 (net tangible assets, operating profit track record, or the QIB route). Check them early.
The reference note says restated financials under Ind-AS. ICDR requires restated financials in line with the accounting framework the company follows; check whether Ind AS applies.
The reference note says SEBI review typically takes 30 to 60 days. This is not a fixed rule. Do not treat it as a deadline.
The reference note lists SH-7 and INC-27 as applicable ROC forms. Name change or alteration of articles may need other forms such as INC-24; check each action.
The reference note lists a monitoring agency above Rs. 100 crore. Confirm the current ICDR limit.

title: Issuing share warrants by a listed company
law: Sections 23, 42 and 62, Companies Act, 2013; SEBI ICDR Regulations, 2018; SEBI LODR Regulations, 2015
summary: Covers a preferential issue of warrants by a listed company, from board approval to allotment and lock-in.
when: A listed public company wants to issue warrants that convert into equity shares on a later date.
applies: Listed public companies, if the articles allow

steps.d: The reference note says only a listed public company can issue share warrants, and only if its articles permit it. It also mentions Central Government approval; see the flags.

Hold a board meeting to approve the warrant issue. File the resolution with the ROC. At the same time tell the stock exchange of the fund-raising proposal under Regulation 30, Part A of Schedule III of SEBI LODR, in the format of the SEBI master circular of 11 November 2024.
steps.time: MGT-14 within 30 days of the resolution

steps.t: Send notice of the general meeting
steps.d: Give 21 clear days' notice stating the number of warrants, price or conversion formula, conversion terms and lock-in, with disclosures under ICDR Regulation 163 and Rule 13 of the Share Capital and Debentures Rules. Send the notice to the stock exchange and put it on the company's website (Regulation 34(1) of LODR).
Obtain a Practising Company Secretary's certificate that the issue meets the ICDR rules. Place it before members at the meeting, host it on the website and give the link in the notice.
Before issuing, get in-principle approval from the stock exchange(s). Where the shares are listed only on exchanges with nationwide terminals, get it from all of them.
Members pass a special resolution at the general meeting. File it with the ROC and send the outcome and scrutiniser's report to the stock exchanges.

If the issue is over Rs. 100 crore, a SEBI-registered credit rating agency must monitor the use of proceeds. It reports each quarter within 45 days of quarter end in Schedule XI format until all proceeds are used.
steps.time: Quarterly, within 45 days of quarter end

steps.d: Set the exercise price based on the volume-weighted average price (VWAP) of the company's shares.
For a preferential offer, send the offer cum application letter in Form PAS-4 to the proposed allottees. One warrant may carry only one security.

Complete allotment within 15 days of the special resolution. If missed, pass a fresh special resolution and take the price relevant date from the new resolution. Take at least 25% of the consideration on allotment of each warrant, and the balance 75% when the equity shares are allotted on exercise. Allot only in demat form.
steps.time: Within 15 days of the special resolution

steps.d: File the return of allotment with the ROC and make a Regulation 30 disclosure to the stock exchanges.
The reference note says lock-in is one month from allotment for promoters and usually six months for others.

forms.purpose: Board resolution and special resolution
Offer cum application letter to allottees
Return of allotment

resolutions.text:

resolutions.title: Allotment of warrants
resolutions.text:
RESOLVED THAT, under the special resolution passed on [date] and the in-principle approval dated [date], [number] warrants be allotted to the persons in the list placed before the meeting, at Rs. [price] per warrant, on receipt of at least 25% of the price (Rs. [amount] per warrant), in dematerialised form.

RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the allotment be intimated to the stock exchanges and Form PAS-3 be filed with the Registrar of Companies, and [name], Company Secretary, be authorised to do so.

docs.title: Intimation to stock exchange of fund raising proposal
paras: To, [BSE Limited / National Stock Exchange of India Limited]. Sub: Intimation under Regulation 30 of SEBI LODR.

We inform you that the board of {co} at its meeting held on [date] approved the issue of up to [number] warrants on a preferential basis at Rs. [price] per warrant, subject to approval of members and the exchange. Meeting began at [time] and ended at [time]. The general meeting is proposed for [date].
For {co}, [name], Company Secretary.

flags: The reference note says Central Government approval is required. The Companies Act, 2013 does not require this for a preferential issue by a listed company; SEBI ICDR and exchange approvals apply. Verify.

The reference note says unlisted public and private companies cannot issue warrants. The Act has no such bar; unlisted companies can issue convertible warrants by private placement (Sections 42 and 62). Verify.
The reference note gives lock-in as one month for promoters. ICDR Regulation 167 now gives 18 months for promoter warrants; check the current rule. Non-promoter lock-in is six months.
The reference note says the exercise price is based on VWAP. ICDR Regulation 164 sets a floor using 90 and 10 trading-day VWAP; check the exact formula.
Allotment must be within 15 days of the resolution, or within 15 days of the last regulatory approval if one is pending. The reference note does not say this.

The reference note omits that warrants must be exercised within 18 months of allotment (ICDR Regulation 169) and does not mention Form PAS-5 and the separate bank account for private placement money; verify.
Step 2 is about the board resolution; also confirm MGT-14 applies to it as the reference note says.
private: An unlisted public company and a private company cannot issue share warrants.

title: Independent director continuing as non-executive director
law: Chapter XI, Companies Act, 2013; Companies (Appointment and Qualification of Directors) Rules, 2014
summary: Moves a director from the independent director role to a non-executive director role: resign, be appointed as additional director, then get members' approval.
when: An independent director wants to stay on the board as a non-executive director.
applies: Companies that have independent directors (not private companies)

steps.d: The director first resigns from the independent director role. The resignation takes effect on the date in the letter or the date the company receives it, whichever is later.
File the resignation with the ROC after it takes effect.
steps.time: Within 30 days of the effective date

steps.d: After resigning, the director gives consent to act as a non-executive director.

Place the proposal before the Nomination and Remuneration Committee, if there is one. On its recommendation, the board appoints the person as additional director (non-executive) to hold office until members approve.
Tell the ROC of the appointment as additional director.
State the terms of appointment and the details required by Section 102 in the notice when seeking approval.
After members approve by ordinary resolution, tell the ROC of the change from additional director to director.

forms.purpose: Resignation as independent director
forms.deadline: Within 30 days of the resignation taking effect

forms.purpose: Appointment as additional director (non-executive)
Change from additional director to director
forms.deadline: Within 30 days of the appointment per the reference note

checklist: Consent to act as non-executive director
Declarations from the director (disclosure of interest, non-disqualification)
Notice with explanatory statement for members' approval
DIR-12 filed three times in time

meetings.title: Board meeting to appoint the additional director
General meeting to approve the appointment as non-executive director
meetings.notice_days: 21 clear days (shorter if 95% of members agree)

resolutions.title: Appointment as additional director (non-executive)
resolutions.text:
RESOLVED THAT the resignation of [name of director] (DIN [DIN]) as an independent director of {co}, effective [date], be noted.

RESOLVED FURTHER THAT, on the recommendation of the Nomination and Remuneration Committee and under Section 161 of the Companies Act, 2013 and the articles of association, [name of director], who has given consent to act, be appointed as an additional director in the non-executive category, to hold office until [the next annual general meeting / date of the general meeting], subject to approval of members.

RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name], Company Secretary, be authorised to file Form DIR-12 and do all things needed.

resolutions.title: Appointment as non-executive director
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT, under Sections 152 and 161 of the Companies Act, 2013, [name of director] (DIN [DIN]), appointed as additional director in the non-executive category, be appointed as a non-executive director of {co}, liable to retire by rotation, on the terms in the explanatory statement.
resolutions.explanatory: Explanatory statement: [name] was an independent director from [date] to [date] and resigned on [date]. The board, on the NRC's recommendation, appointed [him / her] as additional director (non-executive) on [date]. [He / She] has given consent to act and a declaration of no disqualification. Brief profile: [qualification, experience, other directorships, shareholding]. Sitting fees: [details]. The board recommends the resolution.

docs.title: Resignation letter of independent director
paras: To, The Board of Directors, {co}.

I, [name], DIN [DIN], resign from the office of independent director of {co} with effect from [date]. I wish to continue on the board as a non-executive director and will give my consent to act in that role after this resignation takes effect.
I confirm that there are no other material reasons for my resignation. Date: [date]. Place: [place]. [Signature].

flags: The reference note does not mention that a director can also file Form DIR-11 within 30 days of resigning (Section 168).
An additional director holds office only until the next annual general meeting (Section 161(1)), not an open period. Appoint members' approval at or before that meeting.
For a listed company, SEBI LODR Regulation 17(1C) needs members' approval of a new director within 3 months or the next general meeting, whichever is earlier. The reference note does not mention it.
The reference note says the DIR-12 for change in designation falls within 30 days of the appointment; the appointment date here is the date of the members' approval. Verify.
private: The rules on appointing independent directors do not apply to a private company.

title: Allotting shares in demat form and updating capital with depositories
law: Rule 9B, Companies (Prospectus and Allotment of Securities) Rules, 2014
summary: Shows how a private company executes a share allotment with NSDL or CDSL and then updates the other depository if its shares are admitted with both.
when: A private company has allotted shares and needs them credited to the allottee's demat account.
applies: Private limited companies with an ISIN

steps.d: Get an ISIN by admitting the securities with NSDL, CDSL or both. The ISIN stays the same across depositories. Each allottee must have a demat account with a participant of the depository where the allotment is executed.

The board passes a resolution for allotment showing the allottee, nature of allotment (rights, ESOP, private placement, etc.), class and type of shares, face value, issue price and total application money received.
File Form PAS-3. The filed form and its challan must go to the RTA and depository. The RTA may ask for proof of other compliances such as BEN-2, but PAS-3 is mandatory.
steps.time: 15 or 30 days from the board resolution, as stated in the reference note

steps.t: Ask the RTA for the document list
steps.d: The RTA tells you the papers needed, the fees due to the RTA and depositories, and the stamp duty payable. Papers usually include the board resolution, shareholders' resolution if needed, PAS-3 and challan, the depository's Corporate Action Information Form, proof of stamp duty, pari-passu confirmation, share capital reconciliation statement if applicable, and the allottee's DP ID and Client ID.
Pay the RTA and the depository. Send money to the right depository bank account, since separate accounts exist for corporate action fees, stamp duty and annual custody fees.

If the allottee's DP is with NSDL, register on the NSDL issuer portal and create a Maker and a Checker login, each with DSC. The Maker submits the application under Corporate Action (Workflow) with documents, the Checker approves, the RTA reviews, and NSDL executes the allotment and issues a confirmation letter. Shares then show in the demat account.

If the allottee's DP is with CDSL, give the signed documents to the RTA. The RTA uploads them to CDSL, which verifies, executes the allotment and issues a confirmation letter. The company does not file directly with CDSL.

steps.t: Update capital with the other depository
steps.d: If the securities are admitted with both depositories, update the other one with the new paid-up capital. The same documents are usually used again. For NSDL, the Maker submits the capital update (number of allottees and shares), the Checker approves, the RTA confirms, and NSDL issues a letter. For CDSL, the RTA uploads the documents and CDSL issues the letter.

forms.purpose: Return of allotment (mandatory for the corporate action)
forms.deadline: 15 or 30 days per the reference note

forms.purpose: Significant beneficial owner return, which the RTA may ask for

checklist: Allottee demat account with right depository
DP ID and Client ID of allottees
Maker and Checker logins on NSDL portal with DSC

resolutions.title: Allotment of shares in dematerialised form
resolutions.text:
RESOLVED THAT, under Section 62 / Section 42 of the Companies Act, 2013 and the approvals already obtained, [number] equity shares of Rs. [face value] each be allotted at Rs. [issue price] per share (including premium of Rs. [premium]) to [name of allottee], on receipt of Rs. [amount], by way of [rights issue / private placement / ESOP].

RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the shares be allotted in dematerialised form and credited to demat account DP ID [DP ID], Client ID [Client ID], and that [name], Director / Company Secretary, be authorised to file Form PAS-3, sign the Corporate Action Information Form and do all things needed with the depositories and the RTA.

docs.title: Request to RTA for corporate action
paras: To, [name of RTA]. Sub: Allotment of shares in demat form of {co} (ISIN [ISIN]).

We allotted [number] equity shares on [date] and request you to process the corporate action with [NSDL / CDSL]. Please share the document list, fees and stamp duty details. We enclose the board resolution, PAS-3 with challan and other papers.
For {co}, [name], Authorised signatory.

flags: The reference note gives 15 or 30 days for PAS-3, counted from the board resolution. PAS-3 is due within 30 days of allotment (Section 39(4)) and within 15 days for private placement (Section 42(8)); count from the date of allotment, not the resolution.

Rule 9B requires private companies (other than small companies) to issue securities in demat form. Capital Updation is a depository practice and is not stated in Rule 9B itself. Check the depository's circulars.
Stamp duty, fees and portal steps change; verify against the latest depository and RTA instructions.
